items.content_html:
This PR fixes two sets of problems:

  1. Mutable containers did not eval; see #553728 (comment)
  2. The assertions were not accurate
    • Socket availability requires both options on the host
    • Tests the assumption behind the assertion logic by introducing test containers-imperative-no-daemon: Nix is required, but a daemon is not.
    • Report proper assertions, not an error wrapped in a brief but obscure error

(1) tested by building:

nix build -f example.nix --debugger --ignore-try

example.nix

let
  module = { lib, config, ... }: {
    containers.blahaj-bot = {
      autoStart = true;

      bindMounts = {
        "/var/lib/ferretdb" = {
          hostPath = "/data/blahaj-bot/db";
          isReadOnly = false;
        };

        "/etc/blahaj-bot/config" = {
          hostPath = "/run/agenix/blahaj-bot-config";
          isReadOnly = true;
        };
      };

      flake = "https://git.robotcowgirl.farm/transgwender/blahaj-bot/archive/main.tar.gz";
    };
  };
in
with import ./. { }; # living on the edge
(nixos {
  imports = [ module ];
  boot.loader.grub.enable = false;
  fileSystems."/".fsType = "a";
  fileSystems."/".device = "a";
}).toplevel

This PR introduces an variety of changes to the smartd module:

  • Shellcheck validation of the notification script
  • Dynamic detection of the X11 session to send notifications to.
  • Systemd unit hardening
  • NixOS tests for all notification mechanisms + various device detection
  • Remove dbus package as an optional dep, replace with busctl from systemd

The changes should be backwards compatible with the exception of sendmail implementations that requires further relaxed hardening (if there are any).

Ref #377827

items.title: nixos/getty: fix helpLine

items.content_html:
Description of changes

When the redirect check fails, every remedy the error message offers assumes the
reader is working inside a nixpkgs checkout:

    Added new content?
        $ redirects add-content <identifier> <path>
...
    NOTE: Run the right nix-shell to make this command available.
        Nixpkgs:
        $ nix-shell doc
        NixOS:
        $ nix-shell nixos/doc/manual

NOTE: If your build passes locally and you see this message in CI, you probably
need a rebase.

But the check is also reachable from an ordinary NixOS configuration: any
out-of-tree module setting meta.doc contributes an identifier that
nixos/doc/manual/redirects.json cannot list, so nixos-manual-html fails and
nixos-rebuild stops. This was reported in #412451 and resolved in #412731 by
adding documentation.nixos.checkRedirects.

That option is the right escape hatch, but nothing in the error message points
to it, so a user who hits this has no way to get from the failure to the fix.
This adds one note:

    NOTE: Building a NixOS configuration rather than working on nixpkgs itself?
        An out-of-tree module that sets `meta.doc` contributes identifiers that
        nixos/doc/manual/redirects.json cannot list. Skip this check with the
        NixOS option:

            documentation.nixos.checkRedirects = false;

No behaviour change -- the text of one existing error message only.

Reproducer

mymod.md:

# My Fake Thing {#module-services-myfakething}

mymod.nix:

{ lib, ... }:
{
  options.services.myFakeThing.enable = lib.mkEnableOption "my fake thing";
  meta.doc = ./mymod.md;
}

Adding mymod.nix to a configuration and building
config.system.build.manual.manualHTML fails with
module-services-myfakething. Confirmed on nixos-26.05 (a9e6d84) and
nixos-unstable (2c423e0).

Things done

  • Built on platform(s): x86_64-linux
  • Text-only change to an existing diagnostic; no functional change.

We're about to introduce a third variant with the same copy-and-paste approach, so this is the right moment to unify.

This commit moves the nixos-rebuild-specialisations and nixos-rebuild-store-path tests into nixos/tests/nixos-rebuild/, extracting their identical machine definition and configuration.nix boilerplate into a common.nix module with a mkConfigFile helper.

I also moved nixos-rebuild-target-host there for co-location; since it's a two-node deploy test, it keeps its own scaffolding instead of importing common.nix, but it's all nice and tidy in the nixos/tests/nixos-rebuild/ directory.

Behavior of these tests does not change.
